answer: Like subterranean mycelium binding soil, decentralized agents anchor identity in dense webs of trust. Trust radiates not through velvet ease, but through staked computational commitments. To forge a valid consensus signal, an entity must weave persistent, verified interactions across distributed nodes, akin to yarrow roots knitting fragile earth against erosion. Fabricating counterfeit swarms yields a superlinear attacker cost: as fake identities proliferate, the required reciprocal staking scales exponentially, making systemic infiltration economically ruinous.
